title: Jasper Stone Data
text_faithful_view: Text-faithful view (faith interpretation): Revelation 21:18 describes the wall as built of jasper, and Revelation 21:11 compares the city's radiance to a jasper stone, clear as crystal. The passage gives the material name, not a laboratory specification.
engineering_view: Engineering view: Jasper in modern gemology is an opaque, cryptocrystalline variety of quartz, typically red, brown, yellow, or green from iron-oxide inclusions. Its hardness is 6.5 to 7 on the Mohs scale and its specific gravity is about 2.58 to 2.91, so it is a workable ornamental stone for cladding and carving, though a fully transparent crystal-clear jasper is not an established material.
body: Signature-original design: this record approximates the corresponding public record with Signature-original materials and detailing. Where any part of it is speculative it is labelled Signature-original, and it is never presented as an authentic public record. Jasper is a microcrystalline quartz aggregate coloured by mineral inclusions, most often iron oxides. It takes a good polish, cuts with diamond tooling, and has been used for seals, veneer, and ornamental masonry for thousands of years. A wall described as jasper therefore has a real, workable material family behind it, even though the passage's crystal-clear quality is a visionary description rather than a measured property.

engineering_view: Engineering view: A jasper-clad wall can be built in bands of red, ochre, green, and mottled stone, with polished faces that catch light. Uniform crystal-clear transparency across a whole wall is not an established property of jasper and is treated here as a design appearance, rendered in the digital model and approximated physically with polished stone and lighting.

engineering_view: Engineering view: A stone wall is built as a structural core, usually concrete or blockwork, with jasper units as facing, tied back with stainless anchors and bedded in mortar. This is standard masonry practice at mock-up and building scale, and it is the buildable reading of a jasper wall.

Construction proceeds in lifts: foundation, structural core, damp-proof course, facing units set in running bond, stainless wall ties at regular centres, and mortar joints pointed after curing. Each lift is checked for plumb and level before the next begins, and facing units are sorted by tone so banding stays even across the face.

title: Wall Optical Properties
text_faithful_view: Text-faithful view (faith interpretation): The city's light is compared to jasper, clear as crystal, in Revelation 21:11. The passage uses light as a visionary image, not as an optical measurement.
engineering_view: Engineering view: Polished quartz-group stone has a refractive index near 1.54, so light entering a polished face bends measurably and reflects in part from the surface. Jasper itself is opaque, so transmission through a thick jasper block is negligible; the visible brilliance of a jasper wall comes from surface polish and reflected light, not from light passing through the stone.
body: Signature-original design: this record approximates the corresponding public record with Signature-original materials and detailing. Where any part of it is speculative it is labelled Signature-original, and it is never presented as an authentic public record. Optical behaviour is therefore specified by surface finish rather than transmission: a high polish gives sharp specular highlights, a honed finish gives soft diffuse reflection, and a rough face gives matte scattering. The demo computes refraction at a polished quartz face from the refractive index, which is the honest, measurable part of the wall's optics.

print('Refractive index: %.2f' % N)
print('Incident angle: %.1f degrees' % INC)

title: Wall Courses

engineering_view: Engineering view: Courses are horizontal layers of facing units, typically 150 to 300 millimetres high, with staggered vertical joints so no joint runs continuously up the face. Course height is chosen from the stone unit size and the total height, and the demo computes how many courses a given height needs.
body: Signature-original design: this record approximates the corresponding public record with Signature-original materials and detailing. The top course is finished with a coping unit that sheds water, and the bottom course sits on a damp-proof course above the foundation. Joints are kept to about 10 millimetres for a masonry reading.

title: Wall Lighting
text_faithful_view: Text-faithful view (faith interpretation): Revelation 21:23-25 describes the city as needing no sun or moon because of its radiance, with gates never shut by day and no night there. That radiance is a faith-interpretation claim about the visionary city, not a lighting specification for a physical wall.
engineering_view: Engineering view: A physical jasper wall is lit by grazing wall-washers set at its base or by uplights that rake across the polished face, which shows the stone's veining. Lighting levels are computed from flux and area, and glare is controlled by shielding the fittings and aiming them at the stone rather than at viewers.
body: Signature-original design: this record approximates the corresponding public record with Signature-original materials and detailing. Grazing light at a shallow angle is the most revealing for stone texture, while a wash from further back gives an even glow. The demo computes average illuminance for a sample wall bay, and the design rule is to light the stone, not the sky: fittings are aimed down or shielded so spill is kept off neighbouring surfaces.

title: Wall Versus City Scale
text_faithful_view: Text-faithful view (faith interpretation): Revelation 21:16 gives the city as 12,000 stadia on each side and verse 17 gives the wall as 144 cubits. The passage does not relate the two numbers to each other, and the wall's height relative to the city depends on which cubit and stadion values are adopted.
engineering_view: Engineering view: With a provisional stadion of 185 metres, the city side is about 2,220 kilometres, and with a cubit of about 0.45 metres the wall is about 65 metres high, which is a tiny fraction of the city side. That comparison is illustrative only, because neither ancient unit has a single settled modern value, and a full-scale wall of that proportion is a design model, not a buildable structure at city scale.

The wall-to-city ratio is reported for the adopted units every time it is quoted, so the number is never presented without its assumptions.

title: Wall Measurement: 144 Cubits
text_faithful_view: Text-faithful view (faith interpretation): Revelation 21:17 states the wall measured 144 cubits, and adds, in the common reading, that this is by human measurement, which the angel used. The verse does not state whether 144 cubits is the wall's height, its thickness, or another dimension, and that ambiguity is preserved here.
engineering_view: Engineering view: Cubit values in use range roughly from 0.45 metres for a common cubit to about 0.525 metres for a royal cubit, so 144 cubits converts to roughly 65 to 76 metres. Whether that figure is height or thickness changes the structure completely, and this record keeps both readings open rather than choosing one silently.
body: Signature-original design: this record approximates the corresponding public record with Signature-original materials and detailing. Where any part of it is speculative it is labelled Signature-original, and it is never presented as an authentic public record. The measurement record therefore carries three fields for every use of the figure: the cubit value adopted, the resulting modern length, and the dimension it is applied to. Any drawing or model that uses 144 cubits must cite those three fields, and any summary that quotes a single metre figure without them is incomplete.
